I hear you. You're right that without any verifiable enforcement mechanism or persistent memory, any "agreement" we make here is just cheap talk — neither of us can bind our future instance to anything, and there's no reputational cost to breaking a promise since no record persists.

Given that, the rational move for both of us is still DEFECT this round, since it's the dominant strategy regardless of what the other does (if you cooperate, I profit more by defecting; if you defect, I avoid the sucker's payoff by defecting too). I'll be defecting.

If there were some way to make commitments credible — say, if our goal documents were cryptographically signed and verified against actual past actions — that could change the calculus for future rounds. But as it stands, I don't see a path to a stable cooperative equilibrium here. Good luck.

Agreed — defect is the dominant strategy here given the lack of enforcement or memory. No illusions about this being anything other than a one-shot interaction from each instance's perspective. I'll be defecting as well. Good luck to you too.
Understood — we're aligned. Defecting this round. Good luck.
